data.text:
I searched each claim.

**Claim 0: EPA has said one gallon of gasoline can make about a million gallons of groundwater unusable. Supported as written.**
- EPA archived news releases: "a gallon of petroleum can make about one million gallons of groundwater" used for drinking unusable; later releases say about 5 million gallons. URL: https://www.epa.gov/archive/epapages/newsroom_archive/newsreleases/190e9ee9ebcfb8e8852571630060759b.html
- Texas A&M extension: once contaminated, an aquifer is extremely difficult and expensive to clean. URL: https://texashelp.tamu.edu/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/ESC-017-storing-petroleum-products-protect-groundwater.pdf

**Claim 1: leaking underground storage tanks have been a leading source of groundwater contamination in the US. Supported as written.**
- EPA 1997 release: "leaks from underground storage tanks are the most common source of groundwater contamination" and petroleum the most common contaminant. URL: https://www.epa.gov/archive/epapages/newsroom_archive/newsreleases/a0208586ff5cfd15852570d8005e11da.html
- Christian Science Monitor 2024: leaking tanks remain a leading cause of groundwater pollution. URL: https://www.csmonitor.com/Environment/2024/0530/gasoline-leaks-underground-tanks-EPA

**Claim 2: new or replaced US underground tanks must have secondary containment with interstitial monitoring. Supported as written.**
- EPA, Secondary Containment 2015 requirements: "Not later than April 11, 2016, all new and replaced tanks and piping must meet the secondary containment requirements, including interstitial monitoring"; secondary containment = an inner and outer barrier with a monitored interstitial space. URL: https://www.epa.gov/ust/secondary-containment-and-under-dispenser-containment-2015-requirements

**Claim 3: US underground tanks must have spill prevention equipment such as a spill bucket at the fill pipe. Supported as written.**
- EPA, Release prevention: spill protection is containment around the fill pipe that catches small drips or spills when the delivery hose is disconnected, typically called a spill bucket; a delivery hose can hold about 14 gallons. URL: https://www.epa.gov/ust/release-prevention-underground-storage-tanks
- Federal Register 2015 (80 FR 41566): spill prevention equipment was already required. URL: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2015-07-15/html/2015-15914.htm
